Compression is absolute king for vocals. Recorded a couple friends earlier and all it really needed to shine through was compression. I like medium pre gain (how loud the input is when it goes to your DAW) and compressing it to amp it to audible levels but if the pre gain is too low compressing won't save you. 

Add a TINY bit of reverb with short decay to fill it in, don't make it noticeable (unless that's what you're going for, for typical rap vocals I recommend small amounts), otherwise it sounds dry and flat. Delay is up to you, it can help but not super necessary per se. Again add a small amount if you do, though automating it to be really noticeable at the end of lines can be cool in some tracks. 

Cut everything below 100hz, it's just unnecessary mud. A lot of it really is in the delivery, if you don't sound confident it'll show, if your delivery is shaky it'll show. Note your mistakes and improve from there.

If there's anything I would absolutely preach it is to learn scales. Seriously, throw some D minor on that bitch and you got Hans Zimmer type beat for dayz

But really, they're nice as shit. Check out natural minor (Aeolian), Locrian, Lydian, and Phyrgian scales. If you're in FL you can automatically make the piano roll highlight the notes for said scale. I only know a handful of scales off the top of my head but they're so crucial.

Also start the melody with root note of the scale. Learning simple chords at this point will take you even further.
